text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The rise in the central bank's reference rates triggered increases in commercial banks' interest rates.
- The Bucharest stock exchange launches cross deals at Thursday's trading session.
- A Court of Accounts report shows irregulaties in the privatisation of around 500 state companies by the State Ownership Fund.
- The transport, finance and economic reforms ministries okayed purchase of Boeing 737 aircraft by the state-run airline Tarom SA.
- The rate of inflation at the end of 1997 could be 40 percent, the newspaper says.
ADEVARUL
- Central bank governor Mugur Isarescu said the depreciation of the leu would be halted as a programme to encourage exports would reinvigorate the currency.
- The leu stepped over the psychologically sensitive threshold of 5,500 to the dollar on the interbank market.
- Furniture maker Moldomobila SA in eastern town of Iasi will raise the price of its prodcuts by 50 percent.
TINERETUL LIBER
- Romania's Agriculture Minister said food prices would be liberalised in three weeks at the most, with bread staying the only subsidised product.
AZI
- The European Bank for Recontruction and Development is willing to give financial support to telephone company Rom Telecom RA in its further growth and eventual privatisation.
ZIUA

- IMF chief negotiator for Romania Poul Thomsen said inclusion of a social protection package in the government's reform programme was realistic. Application of the reform plan is expected to start by mid-February.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Police caught five foreigners who tried to smuggle more than $100,000 out of Romania.
- Romania's air force made its first test-flight with a recently acquired Hercules C-130 transport plane.

- U.S. President Bill Clinton mentioned Romania for the first time as a possible candidate for early NATO admission in his inauguration speech, saying the country concluded treaties which ended historical tensions with neighbours.
ADEVARUL

- Miners in the coal town of Petrosani ceased protests to demand the release of their leader, Miron Cosma, from prison. Cosma was arrested pending investigations on suspicions of undermining state authority.
CURIERUL NATIONAL

- British Foreign Secretary Malcom Rifkind is expected to arrive for a two-day visit to Romania on January 27. He will discuss bilateral ties and Romania's bid to get British support for its early NATO integration.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- French leading actor Gerard Depardieu said during a 24-hour visit he wanted to invest in Romanian theatre, food and textile industries.
- Some 10 percent of Romanian teenagers have experienced drugs, police General Nicolae Berechet said.
LIBERTATEA
- British homosexual rights group "Out Rage" has asked for an international boycot of Romanian wines due to alleged discrimination against homosexuals in the Balkan country.
- Official data put Romanians who suffer of diabetes at 700,000, but the Diabetics Association says they are three times more numerous, or up to 10 percent of the country's 23 million people.
JURNALUL NATIONAL
- Young Romanians can earn up to three million lei monthly acting as gigolos for foreign female tourists. ($ = 5,567 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
